title: Empirical Bayes estimators of the random intercept in multilevel analysis: Performance of the classical, Morris and Rao version
query: How do different empirical Bayes estimators of the random intercept—classical MLE-based, Morris-corrected, and Rao's ANOVA-based—compare in terms of Bayes risk when the level-1 error variance is unknown, and for what sample sizes do these differences become practically negligible?
